neighbours.label: places in the province of Quebec, strongest on the name Quebec itself (Quebec City, Sherbrooke, Laval, Trois-Rivieres, the Gaspe, the Saguenay); places in other Canadian provinces stay quiet
fire: The ice hotel outside Quebec City opens every January.
Whale-watching tours leave from Tadoussac on the Saguenay.
The university hospital in Sherbrooke is expanding.
Commuters from Laval cross the bridge every morning.
The Gaspe Peninsula is famous for Perce Rock.
The paper mill in Trois-Rivieres closed last year.
Hydro-Quebec built the dams on the La Grande River.
The Quebec government passed a new language law.
quiet: The ice palace outside Winnipeg opens every January.
Whale-watching tours leave from Tofino on the west coast.
The university hospital in Kingston is expanding.
Commuters from Mississauga cross the bridge every morning.
The Bruce Peninsula is famous for the Grotto.
The paper mill in Thunder Bay closed last year.
Ontario Hydro built the dams on the Niagara River.
The Ontario government passed a new education law.

notes: Found by a concept screen (Quebec passages vs matched Ontario passages): >= 0.3 on 4 of 4 Quebec passages (Sherbrooke, Quebec, Laval), < 0.1 on every control. Probing: rural Quebec 0.56, Quebec City 0.53, but Montreal (Canadiens) only 0.12; Acadia 0.13, Paris 0.04, Port-au-Prince 0.10, Ottawa 0.02. Montreal is deliberately left out of the fire sentences because it read low. Near misses keep each frame in Ontario, Manitoba or British Columbia.
